masthead.kicker: Hidden Champions of India / a DeepThought series

headline.text: Krish Biotech Research: eastern India's only GLP-accredited agrochemical CRO, on numbers that jumped sharply between two readings.

subhead.text: A Kolkata-promoted contract research organization with OECD-GLP, NABL and multi-country regulatory accreditation, serving agrochemical and pharma majors' registration testing.

snapshot.label: Revenue
snapshot.source: Tracxn (unreconciled with a much smaller FY23 Tofler figure)

snapshot.label: Certifications
snapshot.value: GLP (NGCMA), NABL/ISO 17025, OECD GLP, CIBRC, CPCSEA, AAALAC, SENASA (Argentina), SENAVE (Paraguay)

p1_engine.eyebrow: A certification base that's clearer than the numbers on top of it

blocks.text: The financial picture has a real, unresolved gap: a Tofler pull for FY23 shows EBITDA down 62.15% year-on-year on a small revenue base, while a more recent Tracxn estimate for FY25 shows ₹100-500 Cr revenue, ₹88.45 Cr PAT, a 49.25% EBITDA margin and 45.09% ROE — a scale of company that doesn't reconcile cleanly with the FY23 figure. Both are reported here as-is; the FY25 figures should be treated as directional, not confirmed.
blocks.source: Tofler (FY23) vs. Tracxn (FY25) — genuinely inconsistent, both cited

blocks.text: What's independently checkable regardless of the financial uncertainty: it holds GLP accreditation from NGCMA (National GLP Compliance Monitoring Authority), describing itself as the first and only GLP-compliant lab in eastern/north-eastern India, plus NABL ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation, OECD GLP compliance, CIBRC recognition, CPCSEA registration, AAALAC voluntary accreditation, and certifications from Argentina's SENASA and Paraguay's SENAVE.

It operates a 100,000 sq ft facility (per its own site; a separate source cites 13,000 sq meters) in Kalyani, West Bengal, with 85-120+ M.Sc./Ph.D.-level staff, and states its studies comply with regulatory requirements of the USA, Brazil, Australia, Argentina and India.

The HVT sheet flags `product_improvement` (its DSIR recognition) as unresolved despite `Verified` review status; its GLP certification renewal was covered in 2025 industry press, a real, dated, independent confirmation of continued accreditation.

insights.point: The field is **growing fast, with the largest single driver directly relevant to Krish Biotech's own focus.**
insights.evidence: Global Agriculture CRO Services market: $10.2-10.89B (2024) to $18.78B by 2029 (11.5%/yr) or $26.2B by 2034 (9.9%/yr). Crop Protection Chemicals — the largest downstream driver — captured >48.7% share of the Agriculture CRO market.

insights.point: **Cost economics are pushing agrochemical majors toward outsourced CROs like this one.**
insights.evidence: The cost to discover a single new agrochemical active ingredient now exceeds $300 million, making full in-house R&D increasingly uneconomical; global majors (BASF, Bayer, Syngenta) already outsource >70% of production/testing work to Europe, China or India.

insights.point: Listed peers in the **broader CRO category show real, achievable margins.**
insights.evidence: Syngene International posted a ~30.6% operating EBITDA margin on ₹3,642 Cr FY25 revenue and explicitly offers acute toxicology packages per OECD/OPPTS guidelines for agrochemical clients — a larger-scale validation that CRO margins in this space can be genuinely strong, consistent with (though not proof of) Krish Biotech's own reported 49.25% figure.

reflect.text: A genuinely independently-accredited GLP lab in a fast-growing outsourcing market, whose own reported financial scale jumped in a way this research pass couldn't reconcile. The certifications are the more trustworthy half of this story right now.

items.title: Multi-residue and antibiotic testing for export commodities
items.body: The HVT sheet's own gap research names this directly: the company has the capability for multi-residue and antibiotic testing on export commodities, currently under-marketed relative to its broader service export activity under the IGST Act.

guesslabel.text: Possibilities, not prescriptions. Which would work, and how much, only Krish Biotech's own data and people can tell. Each is small, made to learn fast.

items.title: Pilot multi-residue testing for one export commodity category
items.body: Pick one export commodity category with known multi-residue/antibiotic testing demand and actively market Krish Biotech's existing capability against it, before a broader marketing push across all commodities.

intro.text: A workflow is the set of steps a company runs to get a result. Below are the generic steps for an agrochemical/pharmaceutical CRO in this segment — a directory-depth pass, not yet confirmed against Krish Biotech's own stated process, so marked generic throughout.

steps: offer GLP/OECD-compliant toxicology, ecotoxicology, residue chemistry, physico-chemical, mutagenicity and environmental-fate studies
compile regulatory dossiers for agrochemical/pharma registration

steps: operate physical lab/field-trial infrastructure sized to study volume
scale instrument throughput and staff headcount to turnaround commitments
ensure data defensibility under regulatory audit
deliver on turnaround speed vs. time-to-market pressure
maintain transparency/responsiveness during multi-year registration dossiers
study contracts/work orders awarded on accreditation status, track record, and cost vs. in-house or Western CRO alternatives
sponsor returns for subsequent dossiers if satisfied

takeaway.text: A genuinely rare accreditation set for eastern India, sitting under a set of financial figures that don't yet add up cleanly across sources. **Verify the numbers before acting on the growth story.**
